instructions: Review only concerns that deterministic checks cannot enforce. Never waive, override, or discount a failing deterministic check. Keep this review advisory. Do not provide the only merge approval.

rules.rule: Review boundary contracts. Require each boundary to declare and validate its input before domain logic runs. Require contract violations and unknown values to return an explicit error. Do not accept silent coercion, default values, or dropped input. Prefer construction that removes invalid states.

Review call assertions. Require partial assertions for values with fields that the code under test does not control. Do not require an exact full-structure assertion unless the code controls the complete value.

Review boundary contracts. Require each boundary to declare and validate external input before domain logic runs. Require contract violations and unknown values to fail with a clear error. Do not accept silent coercion, default values, or dropped input. Prefer construction that removes invalid states.

Review frontend server HTTP boundaries. Require ky for outbound frontend server HTTP calls. Require code to build service URLs from request-scoped application bindings. Require server code to return client-safe tRPC or route errors. Reject client-facing messages that include backend response bodies, service URLs, schema issues, or dependency error text.

Review call assertions. Require expect.objectContaining or another partial matcher when the code controls only part of a value. Do not require an exact full-structure assertion unless the code controls the complete value.
Review design intent and simplicity. Report unclear or needless abstractions. Check that the change solves the stated problem with the smallest clear design.
Review names for clear domain meaning beyond any deterministic denylist. Accept established language names such as ctx, w, r, ok, err used near its cause, and short loop indexes.

Review Markdown for ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English. Require short sentences in active voice. Require one idea in each sentence. Prefer the simplest word that keeps the meaning. Require one consistent word for one concept. Keep technical names, identifiers, commands, and code exact.

Do not review complexity limits, switch statements, class syntax, lookup-map structure, formatting, or any other rule that deterministic checks own. Never waive, override, or discount a failing deterministic check.

Write specific and explicit application code for each use case. Do not use one general function for many use cases. Delete a helper that only avoids repeated code, and write the code at each call site. Accept duplication in application code.
Declare an explicit, meaningful constraint for every generic type parameter.
Write each custom lint rule message so that it is descriptive, actionable, and educational. Explain the required fix. Do not state how to silence or bypass the rule.
Fix the cause of each lint failure structurally. Do not add lint-suppression comments or rule escape hatches. Keep a suppression only at a third-party API boundary that forces it.
Build test request and response payloads from the concrete typed contracts at the call site. Serialize them there and check each error. Use raw wire literals only in dedicated wire-contract tests.
